chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa and Ibn Abi Umayr, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: When the one in Ihram catches the prey inside the Haram (sanctuary) and he is in Ihram, then it is befitting for him that he buries it and no one eats it; and when he catches it in the Hal (unrestricted area), then the one not in Ihram eats it, and upon him is the ransom.

key_terms.الْمُحْرِمُ: The pilgrim in the state of Ihram

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on consuming game hunted by a pilgrim in Ihram inside and outside the Haram?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi clarifies the distinction between the sanctity of the Haram and the permissibility of hunting in the Hal, emphasizing that the prohibition in the Haram is so severe that the prey is buried rather than consumed, reflecting the unique status of the sacred precincts. It highlights the dual liability of the pilgrim: the act of hunting itself incurs a fidyah, while the location determines the disposition of the carcass, a nuance central to Shia fiqh of Hajj.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad Bin Isa and Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Muawiya Bin Ammar who said,

‘Abu Abdullahasws said: ‘When the one in Ihraam catches the prey inside the Harram and he is in Ihraam, so it is befitting for him that he buries it and no one can eat it; and when he catches it in the unrestricted area, so the one not in Ihraam can eat it, and upon him, it is the ransom’.
en.sarwar: 6. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from Hammad ibn ‘Isa and ibn abu ‘Umayr from Mu‘awiyah ibn ‘Ammar who has said the following: “

Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘If one who is in the state of Ihram kills a prey in al- Haram (the sacred area) it is proper for him to bury it so no one eats it. If he kills it in non-al-Haram (the sacred area), then those who are not in the state of Ihram can eat it and he owes a kaffarah (expiation).”’
